- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and slow downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) — add 1-3% bias upward for short-term forecasts.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model delays reaction — forecast should accelerate upward by 1-2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model often ignores sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to reflect 1-2 day lag in reaction to sentiment shifts.  
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion — reduce forecast by 2-5% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
